claims.text: Strong low-field magnetocaloric response in rare-earth-free high-entropy alloys is governed by magnetoelastic coupling enhanced by nanoscale chemical and lattice disorder.
Local lattice distortions and compositional variations create regions with optimized magnetic exchange interactions.
These locally optimized regions rapidly reorient under low applied magnetic fields.
Low-field reorientation of local magnetic moments produces a large magnetic entropy change.
A continuous metallic or crystalline matrix provides high thermal conductivity and rapid heat dissipation.
A continuous metallic or crystalline matrix preserves mechanical strength.
A continuous metallic or crystalline matrix helps maintain low magnetic hysteresis.
The as-cast alloy has high chemical disorder and lattice distortion.
Disorder and lattice distortion in the as-cast alloy produce heterogeneous local magnetic exchange interactions.
Controlled thermal annealing reduces local chemical disorder and lattice distortions.
Annealed samples with reduced nanoscale disorder will exhibit a lower magnetic entropy change below 1 T than the as-cast baseline.
Thermal conductivity will remain comparable or improve after annealing.
Mechanical stability will remain comparable or improve after annealing.
A more uniform matrix structure can improve thermal conductivity or mechanical stability.
The proposed relationship is expected to apply primarily to compositionally similar rare-earth-free high-entropy alloys compared between as-cast and moderately annealed states.
The proposed relationship may not hold for drastically different compositions, processing routes, or disorder changes beyond a moderate level.
